newsitem.title: USA: International Speedway boosts IPO range.
newsitem.headline: International Speedway boosts IPO range.

text.p: International Speedway Corp Monday raised the estimated pricing range for its initial public offering to $18 to $20 a share, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The company had estimated a pricing range of $14 to $16 in its September registration statement.
The offer of 4.0 million shares could be priced as early as Monday night, according to lead underwriter Smith Barney.

The Daytona Beach, Fla.-based motor sports promoter is best known for its superspeedways and the Daytona 500 race, held under the auspices of the National Association of Stock Car Auto Racing Inc (NASCAR).
The company is currently traded on a limited basis as a bulletin board stock under the symbol ISWY.OB. It closed at $370 a share at its last trade on November 1.
The shares to be offered in the initial public offering form a new class of stock to be traded on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ISCA."
International Speedway's profits and revenues increased about 25 percent last year, the company said.
Some 5.3 million fans attended NASCAR's Winston Cup races, up 8.8 percent from the previous year.
The descendants of Bill France Sr, the patriarch of American stock-car racing who died in 1992, will control the company.
